answers.workaround:
The workaround I'm currently using is a setup where a I have an array of `rendering_noise_textures` where all textures are added when I believe they will start their rendering, and then a system that subscribes to the texture `changed` signal, binding the specific texture to this signal. When this is emitted the texture is removed from the `rendering_noise_textures`. This way I can tell if generation is still waiting for any rendering textures or if a specific texture is finished or not by inspecting my `rendering_noise_textures` array.

However, this system is a little convoluted to set up and you might easily miss cases by putting textures on the watch list or subscribing to the change signals at the wrong time, or removing them incorrectly as finished if the texture emits a `changed` signal due to some other change during texture setup.

So having a dedicated `is_rendering` flag to check and a dedicated `finished_rendering` signal would make this easier to get right every time as well as allow making more use of the parallel rendering for performance.

title: Add is_rendering property on NoiseTexture2D/3D that indicates if it is still rendering and a dedicated finished_rendering signal
